title: Failover Testing: The Complete Beginner's Guide

scenes.narration: A fire drill tests that people can leave the building. Your network needs the same kind of test. Does the backup really take over?

scenes.heading: Fire drill for your network
scenes.narration: Backups are only useful if they actually work. Pull the plug on the main router and watch what happens. H S R P says hello every three seconds, with a ten second hold. V R R P advertises every second, with about three seconds before takeover. Write down how long it took, and compare with your target.

items.real: Under a second is the goal for FHRPs

scenes.heading: Common mix-ups
scenes.narration: Three tips. Untested redundancy is a guess. Schedule tests as changes. Retest after any change.

scenes.heading: Remember this
scenes.cta: Try the Courseiva failover testing lab
scenes.narration: So, to recap. Test your backups before you need them. Know the default timers. Write down how long failover takes. Ready to practise? Try the Courseiva failover testing lab.
